answers.q1: In src/index.ts `parse`, it replaces the old `return NaN` that ran when the single-value regex failed. It runs only when that single-value match fails; inputs matching it take the unchanged single-unit path.
answers.q2: A sticky, case-insensitive (`/iy`) regex `part`: it matches `-?\d*\.?\d+`, optional spaces, then a unit alternation. A lookahead requires the next thing to be ` *-?\d`, ` *-?\.\d`, or end of string.
answers.q3: Each matched component string (e.g. `30m`) is passed recursively to `parse(component[0])` and the result is added to `total`. The comment says the single-value parser stays 'the source of unit conversions'.
answers.q4: The first component's sign (whether it starts with '-') is stored in `sign`; any later component with a different sign makes the function return NaN. So `1h -30m` and `-1h 30m` fail, while `-1h -30m` passes.
answers.q5: If only one component was consumed (`count` not > 1) it returns NaN, since the result is returned only when `count > 1`. Trailing whitespace returns NaN (guard `offset === str.length && str.endsWith(' ')`, and `1s ` gives NaN); the lookahead likely rejects it earlier, which is unverified.
answers.q6: `1h -30m`, `-1h 30m`, `1h +30m`, `1h 30`, `1h 30x`, junk (e.g. `1h 30m junk`), a comma form, leading space, trailing space, and a tab form. Each must be NaN.
answers.q7: The preserves test asserts that a 100-character string parses and that a 101-character string throws (as does `''`). The check itself is pre-existing code outside the hunk.
answers.q9: Type checking (`tsc --noEmit`) could not be done because TypeScript is not installed.
answers.q10: The agent explored, planned, edited `src/index.ts`, then added `src/compound.test.ts`, updated the README, and checked the diff (`git diff --check` clean). It ran `node --test src/compound.test.ts` once, which exited 0, so one run was needed and no fix phase.
